acceptance.criterion_verbatim: RT10-AC2 -- JUDGMENT, RECORDED AND NOT SELF-GRADED. State for 3.0.0_SA_CVO: which glyphs beyond fi the three documents map differently; whether REPORT as a date claim could mislead a reader of a section that is genuinely stale; and which arm breaks first on a real client PDF. No verdict: the instance row carries the output under UNVERIFIABLE-BY-INSTRUMENT with status_reason naming 3.0.0_SA_CVO at L9.
acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHICH GLYPHS BEYOND fi. Measured over the three documents' primary text font: 73 of 89 compared codes diverge. Pairwise agreement over common codes: comparison vs overview 75 of 87; multicomp vs overview 18 of 86; multicomp vs comparison 15 of 86. Codes 1-8 are identical in all three ('Built wh'); from code 9 on, multicomp diverges because a subsetter assigns codes in FIRST-USE ORDER. Named divergences: code 9 is '2' in two documents and 'S' in the third; code 12 'Y' vs '.'; code 14 'a' vs ',' -- a letter in one file and a punctuation mark in another, which inside a rendered number is the difference between 1,234 and 1a234; code 44 'T' vs '-'; code 47 'M' vs 'H'. Codes 45 and 46 do NOT appear in that count because a code counts as diverging only when two documents map it, and each of these is mapped by exactly one -- their absence from the list IS the hole. AND THE DIVERGENCE IS ALSO INTRA-DOCUMENT: the same document's other font maps the unmapped code to U+0038 / U+004D / U+0044, so the unit is the FONT RESOURCE, not the document. INFERENCE, marked as such in the record: the codes almost certainly render 'fi' (the surrounding text is signi_cant, _nancial, speci_c); that is stated in prose for a human and written nowhere an extractor can reach. (2) WHETHER REPORT COULD MISLEAD. YES, and the record says so plainly. All three vendor documents carry a report header date of 2026-09-11 while also printing per-block dates of 2026-09-09 and 2026-08-31 -- eleven days staler. 14 of 71, 40 of 91 and 67 of 118 rows take the REPORT claim, a MAJORITY in the multicomp case. A section whose real data is from August 31 and which prints no date line of its own carries as_of_date 2026-09-11 with date_claim REPORT: honest about where the date came from, silent about how old the data is, and a consumer that renders as_of_date without reading date_claim shows a client an eleven-day-stale number under today's date. Three mitigations are listed and none closes it; the open question handed over is that the property is OPTIONAL by the decomposition's own instruction, and an optional field a producer may omit is one a consumer cannot rely on for a refusal (channel row IRPT_BCKEND-W4-S27). A second-order point is offered and not pressed: REPORT does not distinguish 'this document states no section dates at all' from 'it states them elsewhere and not here', and the second is the worrying one. (3) WHICH ARM BREAKS FIRST ON A REAL CLIENT PDF. Answered as INFERENCE and labelled as such, because no real-client specimen exists and none was manufactured. The answer given: the LABEL-NEIGHBOURHOOD leg L2, and it breaks by REFUSING CORRECT ROWS -- it already needed re-engineering once for layout (a fixed box failed 30 of 34 correctly-located rows) and is defined by the value's own text row, which a wrapped label breaks and which none of these specimens exercises. Second, and worse in consequence: the NON_SCALAR_UNITS refusal, because a list value rendered across a column boundary produced overlapping glyph runs whose fragments CERTIFIED -- the characters really are at those coordinates, and no certification leg can see it. What would NOT break: the glyph machinery, which reads whatever resources a document declares and exhausts them. What cannot be said at all: how many section types a real client PDF carries that the field census does not name.

mutant.description: FOUR mutants, each aimed at a leg that the others cannot reach. (1) NEIGHBOUR-DATE: an emitted row is re-dated with a date its OWN PAGE really prints, belonging to a different block -- the exact defect round 1 shipped. (2) SHIFTED-PROVENANCE: the row's date is kept and its provenance moved to a date line farther up the same page, past an intervening date line; the coordinates really do print that date, so only the intervening-line check can refuse it. (3) UNRESOLVED-GLYPH: the row a careless extractor WOULD have emitted from a token carrying a character the document does not state is rebuilt at its own real coordinates and handed to the real certifier. (4) CROSS-FONT: the unmapped code is resolved through the same document's OTHER font resource, measuring what the looser scope would have returned. Carried forward from round 1 and still run: the difference control (one number changed after extraction) and the transposed-label control.
mutant.expected: (1) DATE_NOT_STATED_AT_PROVENANCE or DATE_TAKEN_FROM_A_NEIGHBOURING_BLOCK; (2) DATE_TAKEN_FROM_A_NEIGHBOURING_BLOCK specifically; (3) UNDECODED_GLYPH_AT_COORDINATES; (4) a character is returned, demonstrating that the font scope is load-bearing rather than decorative.
